properties.address: 1 W Register St, Edinburgh EH2 2AA, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock: Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Inverclyde and Strathclyde Groups, featuring Calciferous Sandstone measures overlain by glacial till. Primary architectural lithics: pale carboniferous Craigleith and Hailes sandstones (fine-to-medium quartz arenite), with Cullalo and Clashach sandstone in restorative phases. Mortar: historic non-hydraulic lime-sand mixes with carbonaceous particulate inclusions.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban civic parkland containing *Acer pseudoplatanus* (sycamore), *Tilia cordata* (small-leaved lime), and *Ulmus glabra* (wych elm). Late September phenology: dense canopies exhibiting early foliar chlorosis, patchy yellowing, and minor outer-canopy defoliation. Interior central lawn composed of perennial *Lolium perenne* and *Poa pratensis* turf.

properties.architectural_summary: Georgian New Town urban plan centered on an elliptical garden enclosure. Centerpiece: Melville Monument (42-metre fluted Roman Doric column atop a rusticated square plinth). Surrounding perimeter: 4-to-6-storey Georgian Classical and Victorian Palazzo-style ashlar commercial frontages, punctuated by late-20th-century concrete frame and modern glass-and-steel commercial infill. Roofscapes feature timber rafter profiles, Ballachulish slate pitches, lead-dressed dormers, and ashlar chimney stacks. Fenestration: 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 timber sash-and-case grids alongside modern planar curtain-wall glazing.
